title: Trace function of a Weil complex
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and the fixed algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\Ql=\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $X_0$ be a separated finite-type $k_0$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$. Let $K$ be a $\Qlb$-Weil complex [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Its underlying coefficient object may be written in the PBC common-stage category [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]: throughout, this means transport of the entire Weil pair along the equivalence $J_X$ of [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], including its specified comparison with geometric-Frobenius pullback. For local evaluation, use the corresponding pair in the framework category [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients].

For $n\geq1$ and $x\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})$, take the geometric point $\bar x$ induced by the specified inclusion $\mathbf F_{q^n}\subset k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. The *trace function* is the function $t_{K,n}:X_0(\mathbf F_{q^n})\to\Qlb$, also written $t_K(x)$ when $n$ is understood, defined by
$$
 t_K(x)=\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid K_{\bar x}\bigr)
 =\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_x^{(n)}\mid\mathcal H^j(K)_{\bar x}\bigr).
$$
The local operators, point-complex interpretation of the cohomology stalks, and alternating-trace convention are those of [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace]; each summand uses ordinary linear trace [def-weil-endomorphism-trace]. Concretely, choose a finite coefficient-field Weil model $(E,V_E)$ of the framework pair, compute the displayed finite alternating sum in $E$, and include its value along $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$.

Such a model is obtained by representing the underlying object, the Weil isomorphism, its inverse and their two inverse equations over one finite extension. The common-stage calculus [prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus], transported through the coefficient-system equivalence [lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison], supplies this simultaneous representation; the specified pullback comparison in [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex] identifies its source with the finite-stage Frobenius pullback. Two such models become isomorphic as Weil pairs over a common further finite extension: represent the comparison, its inverse, the inverse equations and the Weil-intertwining equation there. By [lem-fd-local-weil-model-trace-independence] their included ordinary traces agree in each degree. Only finitely many degrees contribute by [def-weil-local-frobenius-trace], so the included alternating sums agree. Thus the displayed prescription is independent of the finite-stage Weil model. If the first trace is read categorically on the point complex, [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws](4) identifies it with the same displayed sum.

lean.statement: def weilTraceFunction [IsSeparated X₀.hom] (K : sfCommonStageWeilComplex D l hl X₀ Qbar) (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) (x : D.extensionPoints X₀ n hn) : Qbar
lean.note: The old WeilSheaf.traceFunction record only treats sheaves and does not expose the source common-stage adic Weil-complex interface. This module defines the Qbar-valued trace of every sfCommonStageWeilComplex by the uniquely specified inclusion of localExtensionTrace at every finite-stage Weil model. The named existence/uniqueness theorem postpones precisely well-definedness of this definition; its proof plan descends the Weil isomorphism and its inverse and uses conjugacy and scalar invariance of ordinary traces.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NS-715d1463d (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes, every flagged node and every node my checks rely on. The item keeps the source's domain (separated finite-type X0, n>=1, every Qbar-Weil complex) and formula, adds no hypothesis, and transports the whole Weil pair (object, theta and the Frobenius comparison) from the framework category to def-weil-pbc-qbar-category; it never treats the two categories as equal. Finite models come from the statement of prop-weil-pbc-common-stage-calculus; X is noetherian and finite-dimensional and ell is invertible on it. lem-fd-rational-coefficient-category-comparison is true: the integral characterization says the two integral categories are the same full subcategory; both rational categories are the raw Hom tensor E with no Karoubi completion; the scalar-extension comparison is the rationalized chi^{-1}; and both pullbacks are Rlim of the same finite-reduction tower, with g_X an automorphism. lem-fd-local-weil-model-trace-independence: I checked the types of b; the intertwining identity follows from point-transport naturality and its scalar compatibility (lem-weil-frobenius-point-transport-natural (2)), the coherence equation of the pullback realization lemma, and iterating the Weil-intertwining equation; then cohomology commutes with scalar extension and ordinary traces are conjugation- and scalar-invariant. Tests: rank one with eigenvalues alpha and alpha', where the hypothesis forces alpha=alpha'; an arbitrary u is excluded; zero and shifted complexes; E=L. Neither new node duplicates an existing one (nodes citing both coefficient systems and the local-conjugacy nodes were checked), and neither restates a clause of the item. The previously rejected lem-trf-local-frobenius-transport-normalization and prop-trf-karoubi-independence are no longer cited. Neither assumption leaf gives any of these, none is a specific step of the trace-formula or Poincare-duality proof, and all were accepted. prop-trf-trace-formal-laws(4) is exactly what the scope note of nt-assume-trace-formula excludes.
